description:
If you are buying a flat, or already own one, there is a number in the brochure worth checking twice.

Most brochures quote "super built-up area". It counts the floor inside your home, and also your walls and your share of the lobby, lifts, stairs and clubhouse. The extra part is called loading, and it is often around 30 percent. So a flat sold as 1,200 sq ft may have only about 920 sq ft of floor you can actually walk on. Under RERA, the carpet area is the legal measure, so it is fair to ask the builder for it in writing.

When you bought your home, did anyone tell you the carpet area?

(Example with 30% loading; it varies by project. Sources: RERA Act 2016, ICICI Bank, Business Standard 11 Jun 2026. Some scenes are AI visualisation. For education only.)
